subject: Cloud Computing
title: Oracle Cloud's Late Bet
description: A quick, practical guide to Oracle Cloud's Late Bet.

hook.text: Oracle mocked cloud computing for years. Then it scrambled to build its own cloud — a decade late.

buildup.text: Larry Ellison dismissed cloud as 'complete gibberish' in 2008. By 2016, Oracle was racing to catch up.

discovery.text: Oracle Cloud targeted its massive existing database customer base: migrate your Oracle DB to our cloud.

twist.text: Oracle scored a surprise win: TikTok chose Oracle Cloud for U.S. data, boosting its credibility overnight.

climax.text: Oracle Cloud remains a niche player. But in databases, it competes fiercely with services no one else offers.

punchline.text: Oracle arrived late. Its database customers gave it a foothold.

quiz.question: How did Oracle Cloud gain initial traction despite launching late?
options: By targeting its existing database customers with migration incentives
By offering the cheapest cloud services in every category
By buying AWS and rebranding its services

details.summary: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure launched later than competitors but invested aggressively in second-generation cloud architecture and competitive pricing. Oracle targets its massive database customer base and has won high-profile customers by offering superior price-performance for database workloads.
details.whyItMatters: Oracle's late entry proves that cloud market share is not permanently fixed. By targeting database workloads where it has deep expertise, Oracle carved out a profitable niche.
takeaways: Oracle built second-generation cloud architecture from scratch
Competitive pricing undercuts AWS for database workloads
Oracle targets its existing database customer base for migration

faq.question: What is Oracle Cloud's advantage?
faq.answer: Oracle Cloud offers native Oracle Database support with performance that exceeds running Oracle on AWS or Azure. Free egress pricing, dedicated region offerings, and aggressive pricing attract cost-conscious customers. Autonomous Database provides self-managing database capabilities.

faq.question: Can Oracle Cloud compete with AWS and Azure?
faq.answer: Oracle does not need to match AWS's breadth to succeed. By dominating the Oracle Database workload niche and offering competitive general-purpose infrastructure, Oracle Cloud has grown revenue significantly. Its partnership with Microsoft for cross-cloud connectivity also extends its reach.
